_doc: Vikriti estimation rules. Each rule: conditions evaluated against current-state features {heart_rate, sleep_hours, sleep_quality, stress, energy, activity, mood, symptoms}; effect adds points to a dosha (capped by max_points_per_dosha). point_scale converts rule points into raw percentage points before normalization. tendency_thresholds define the arrow thresholds (in percentage points) vs baseline. All mappings are classical Ayurvedic-inspired wellness heuristics, NOT clinical thresholds. Edit freely — loaded at request time.

rules.explanation: Short sleep duration (under ~6 hours) is classically linked to Vata elevation.
Poor sleep quality combined with high stress contributed to the Vata-oriented score.
High reported stress is classically associated with Vata aggravation.
The elevated heart rate you entered was treated as a heat/agitation signal (Pitta) — a transparent proxy, not a clinical measure.
A very high entered heart rate added further Pitta weighting.
Irritability is classically associated with Pitta aggravation.
Anxious or restless mood is classically associated with Vata aggravation.
A low mood was treated as a mild heaviness signal (Kapha).
A sluggish mood is classically associated with Kapha aggravation.
Low energy contributed to a Kapha (heaviness) signal.
A highly active day added small Pitta (heat) and Vata (overexertion) signals.
Low physical activity contributed to a Kapha (inertia) signal.
Sleeping more than ~9 hours is classically associated with Kapha aggravation.
Bloating is classically associated with Vata aggravation.
Gas is classically associated with Vata aggravation.
Constipation is classically associated with Vata aggravation.
Dry skin is classically associated with Vata aggravation.
Restlessness is classically associated with Vata aggravation.
Acidity is classically associated with Pitta aggravation.
Heartburn is classically associated with Pitta aggravation.
Headache (heat-type) was treated as a mild Pitta signal.
Loose stools are classically associated with Pitta aggravation.
Congestion is classically associated with Kapha aggravation.
Sluggishness is classically associated with Kapha aggravation.
Heavy body ache was treated as a mild Kapha signal.
